source.branch: A horizontal WAN_STRIKING zap reaches a live monster and a floor pile on the same square. The Healer’s starting kitten is killed by the hit at step 40; after the More prompt, step 41 key Space resumes the ray and bhito() receives the resulting kitten corpse. Since svc.context.mon_moving is false, bhito() calls hero_breaks(obj, ox, oy, 0). breaktest() rolls ordinary-object resistance with nonbreakchance=1; the recorded rn2(100)=3 is not a resistance, but CORPSE is neither glass nor one of breaktest()’s breakable types, so breaktest() and hero_breaks() return 0. bhito() suppresses learning, leaves the corpse in place, sets res=0, and returns 0. The other Force Bolt branches (boulder, statue/break_statue, and monster-caused breaks()) are distinct and are not evidenced by this object.
callers: nethack-c/upstream/src/cmd.c:2004-2005 dispatches z to zap.c:dozap(); zap.c:2673 calls weffects() after the wand is selected and aimed.

nethack-c/upstream/src/zap.c:3431-3451 routes this horizontal IMMEDIATE wand to bhit(..., ZAPPED_WAND, bhitm, bhito, ...). bhit() calls bhitm() first; its Force Bolt branch returns 0 after the kitten death, so the ray continues to bhitpile().

nethack-c/upstream/src/zap.c:2428-2505 calls bhito() for each floor object and adds its return to hitanything. zap.c:4045-4048 consumes bhitpile()’s result to decide whether to shorten the ray; weffects() discards bhit()’s monster-pointer return.

The corresponding JS path is js/cmd.js:3328-3329 runZapCommand() -> js/zap.js:dozap() -> weffects() -> bhit() -> bhitm()/bhitpile() -> bhito(). js/zap.js:2906-2910 is the immediate stop site; bhitpile() sums the callback result at :3131 and bhit() uses that sum at :3433-3434.
dependencies: dothrow.c:hero_breaks() returns 0 when breaktest() says the object will not break; when it passes, breakmsg() precedes breakobj(), whose result is propagated. breaktest() at :2582-2609 calls zap.c:obj_resists() and then checks glass material and the explicit breakable-object cases. For this ordinary kitten corpse, obj_resists(obj, 1, 99) consumes the recorded rn2(100)=3 and returns false, but the material/type tests still make breaktest() false. breaks() is the alternative monster-caused entry and is not used because svc.context.mon_moving is false.

The separate STATUE arm in zap.c:bhito() consumes break_statue()’s boolean to decide whether to print the shatter message. break_statue() returns false when a statue trap activates and true after dropping contents, applying the historic-statue alignment effect if applicable, and fracturing the statue. This recording has a CORPSE, not a STATUE, so that return path remains unverified.

The previous step’s bhitm() Force Bolt result and bhito()’s object result are both consumed by zap.c:bhit(): a zero monster result keeps the ray moving and subtracts three from range; a zero bhitpile result does not subtract another range unit. The C result from resist() itself is discarded by bhitm(); its lethal side effects now match through step 40.
